During IRL discussion with @x4m we decided not to implement pause/resume for session pooling. So I am not sure what "for all storages" operation should do. Should it silently apply change only to storages with transaction pooling or report problems with session pooling storages or not work at all if any session pooling storage found?
After more discussions we decided to implement it. This way there will be no problems in changing pooling mode during puase.

We have our internal sleeplock.
It's there for inlining locks.

Actually, I'm not a big fan of bicycles, but, as long as it's already there, let's use it.
I could not find any other lock. And other objects are locked with pthread_mutex_lock too. Could you give a link to certain file/line?
this file is included inside `<odyssey.h>`

I suggest to move this lock and state out of rule type. Rule type is static and versional. If you want to update any rule value you have to create a new rule object. This is how it is done during online config file reload, so existing clients can continue to work with previous rule version. Only `system` can update rules for now.

The better candidate to do it is `route_t` object. Yet it is needed carefully done for dynamic routes, since they can be removed by cron, if there are no existing connections.
I suggest to set `storage_name` to NULL instead of passing it as a an empty string. This can be used as a flag instead of pause all as well.
Please do not use camel case style

Parsing logic here is a slightly incomplete and have a room for errors. This should expect PARSER_EOF token, otherwise it is possible to pass anything like `PAUSE 1234` and it will treat it as pause all condition.

Also I suggest to follow style convention and start log messages from lowercase letter and remove `...`.
Same parsing issues as described above.
